SOCIAL STUDIES — MOCK EXAM #3
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A pupil faces the rising sun in the morning. Which direction is on the pupil's right hand? (1 mark)
   A. West
   B. East
   C. South
   D. North

2. In the morning, your shadow falls towards which direction? (1 mark)
   A. East
   B. West
   C. Nowhere
   D. The sun

3. What does a map key explain? (1 mark)
   A. The date of the map
   B. The meaning of the colours and symbols
   C. The name of the map maker
   D. The weather

4. On the county map in the lesson, the neighbour drawn on the right side is in which direction from the county? (1 mark)
   A. South
   B. East
   C. West
   D. North

5. On a physical map, what colour is often used for high mountains? (1 mark)
   A. Blue
   B. Brown
   C. Pink
   D. White

6. Which of these is built by people, not natural? (1 mark)
   A. A river
   B. A hill
   C. A dam
   D. A plain

7. Which symbol on a weather chart shows rain? (1 mark)
   A. A yellow sun
   B. A cloud with lines falling from it
   C. A plain cloud
   D. A thermometer

8. Where should you shelter during a thunderstorm? (1 mark)
   A. In a strong building
   B. Under a tall tree
   C. Beside a river
   D. In an open field

9. Which of these is not a historic built environment? (1 mark)
   A. A natural river
   B. A cultural centre
   C. A monument
   D. A museum

10. Which statement is true? (1 mark)
   A. Small jobs do not matter
   B. Only farming is important
   C. All useful jobs are important
   D. Only doctors are important

11. How do religious leaders help the community? (1 mark)
   A. They repair roads
   B. They drive buses
   C. They sell food
   D. They teach values and comfort people

12. Which pattern describes houses standing close together around a trading centre? (1 mark)
   A. Linear
   B. Scattered
   C. Clustered
   D. Empty

13. Why do some herding communities use portable dome-shaped houses? (1 mark)
   A. They are very tall
   B. They are made of concrete
   C. They can be moved when the family moves
   D. They cannot be moved

14. Which is a traditional food eaten in many parts of Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Pizza
   B. Ugali
   C. Hamburger
   D. Sushi

15. Which statement about culture is true? (1 mark)
   A. Only one culture is right
   B. Every community's culture deserves respect
   C. Culture never changes
   D. Culture is only about clothes

16. Why do schools have rules? (1 mark)
   A. To stop friendship
   B. To make pupils sad
   C. To keep everyone safe and help learning
   D. To stop lessons

17. Where might you see a school motto? (1 mark)
   A. In a river
   B. On the badge or gate
   C. On a rain cloud
   D. In the sky

18. Where is titanium mined in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Kisumu
   B. Nakuru
   C. Nyeri
   D. Kwale

19. Keeping cattle, goats and camels in dry areas is called what? (1 mark)
   A. Mining
   B. Pastoralism
   C. Trading
   D. Fishing

20. Which activity involves growing crops and keeping animals? (1 mark)
   A. Farming
   B. Tourism
   C. Mining
   D. Fishing

21. How do industries help farmers? (1 mark)
   A. They stop rain
   B. They teach only
   C. They cut farms
   D. They buy the farmers' produce

22. Why are sugar factories usually built near cane farms? (1 mark)
   A. Cane is heavy and costly to carry far
   B. Sugar cannot be sold
   C. Farmers do not like factories
   D. Cane is hard to find

23. Which action shows responsibility? (1 mark)
   A. Refusing to help
   B. Waiting to be told each time
   C. Doing your class duty without being reminded
   D. Breaking things

24. Who can be a role model? (1 mark)
   A. A teacher or an elder
   B. Only a president
   C. Only a rich person
   D. Nobody

25. Which of these is a good digital citizen habit? (1 mark)
   A. Sending mean messages
   B. Sharing passwords
   C. Asking an adult before going online
   D. Talking to strangers

26. Which of these spoils peace? (1 mark)
   A. Listening
   B. Forgiveness
   C. Fairness
   D. Bullying

27. Which day is the International Day of Peace? (1 mark)
   A. 12 December
   B. 25 December
   C. 21 September
   D. 1 January

28. In an election, 12 pupils voted for Amina and 10 for Brian. Who wins? (1 mark)
   A. Amina
   B. Brian
   C. Both
   D. Nobody

29. What are tally marks used for? (1 mark)
   A. Cooking
   B. Counting votes
   C. Measuring rain
   D. Painting

30. Which is a function of the Children's Government? (1 mark)
   A. Beating pupils
   B. Setting exams
   C. Helping to keep order and cleanliness
   D. Collecting fees

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. What is a school motto? (2 marks)

32. State three industries found in Kenya and the raw material each uses. (3 marks)

33. Explain three rules of good digital citizenship. (3 marks)

34. List four ways of caring for rivers and lakes. (4 marks)

35. Explain why it is important to have a Children's Government in school. (4 marks)

36. Describe how a pupil can help a new pupil to settle in. (3 marks)

37. The sugar factory employs 700 workers and the tea factory employs 400 workers. How many workers are there in the two factories together? Show your working. (3 marks)

38. Explain how a class representative helps classmates. (3 marks)

39. Give two examples of natural resources. (2 marks)

40. Give three questions to ask when choosing a school enterprise project. (3 marks)

41. Name two landforms and two water features. (4 marks)

42. Give four services provided by county governments. (4 marks)

43. Explain what may happen in a community with dishonest leaders. (3 marks)

44. Describe five actions that show good citizenship in school. (5 marks)

45. Name four roles in a school enterprise team and state one duty for each. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — MOCK EXAM #3 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — South
   Facing east, south is on the right hand.

2. B — West
   The sun is in the east in the morning, so shadows point west.

3. B — The meaning of the colours and symbols
   The key tells what each line, colour and symbol stands for.

4. B — East
   When north is at the top, the right side is east.

5. B — Brown
   Brown shows high land such as mountains.

6. C — A dam
   A dam is built by people to hold water.

7. B — A cloud with lines falling from it
   Falling lines under a cloud show rain.

8. A — In a strong building
   Lightning can strike tall trees, so a building is safer.

9. A — A natural river
   A river is a natural feature, not built by people.

10. C — All useful jobs are important
   Every worker contributes to the community.

11. D — They teach values and comfort people
   Religious leaders teach good values and care for people.

12. C — Clustered
   Clustered means close together in a group.

13. C — They can be moved when the family moves
   Portable houses suit families who move with their animals.

14. B — Ugali
   Ugali is widely eaten in Kenya.

15. B — Every community's culture deserves respect
   We must respect all cultures.

16. C — To keep everyone safe and help learning
   Rules protect people and help learning.

17. B — On the badge or gate
   Mottos are often on badges and gates.

18. D — Kwale
   Titanium is mined in Kwale County.

19. B — Pastoralism
   Pastoralism is keeping livestock on natural pasture.

20. A — Farming
   Farming is growing crops and keeping livestock.

21. D — They buy the farmers' produce
   Factories need farm produce as raw materials.

22. A — Cane is heavy and costly to carry far
   Being near saves transport costs.

23. C — Doing your class duty without being reminded
   Responsible pupils do their duties.

24. A — A teacher or an elder
   Ordinary people can be good role models.

25. C — Asking an adult before going online
   Asking permission keeps you safe.

26. D — Bullying
   Bullying hurts and frightens people.

27. C — 21 September
   The International Day of Peace is on 21 September.

28. A — Amina
   12 is more than 10.

29. B — Counting votes
   Tally marks help count votes.

30. C — Helping to keep order and cleanliness
   Leaders help with order and cleanliness.

SECTION B
----
31. (2 marks)
   Answer: A motto is a short sentence that shows what a school stands for or hopes to achieve.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for short sentence, 1 mark for showing what the school stands for.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: Sugar factory uses sugarcane, tea factory uses tea leaves, cement factory uses limestone.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each industry with its material.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: Ask an adult before going online, do not share private information, and be kind and never bully online.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

34. (4 marks)
   Answer: Do not throw rubbish into them, plant trees on the banks, do not wash or farm too close to the water, and tell adults about pollution.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

35. (4 marks)
   Answer: It gives pupils a voice, teaches leadership, helps teachers with order and cleanliness, and teaches democracy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: Welcome the pupil, show the classrooms and toilets, and invite the pupil to play.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: 1,100 workers.
   Working / marking points: 700 + 400 = 1,100. 1 mark for adding, 1 mark for correct sum, 1 mark for the unit.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: They bring classmates' ideas and complaints to meetings, tell the class what was decided, and help solve small problems.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

39. (2 marks)
   Answer: Water and soil. Accept forests, minerals, wildlife or fish.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each example.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: Do people want it? Do we have the materials and skills? Is it safe? Can we earn more than we spend?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible question.

41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Landforms: mountain and valley (or hill, plain, plateau). Water features: lake and river (or waterfall, ocean).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct example.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: Health centres, county roads, pre-primary schools and markets. Accept cattle dips or water services.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each service.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Resources are wasted, people lose trust, and people quarrel.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

44. (5 marks)
   Answer: Arrive on time, keep the compound clean, respect teachers, share with others, and report bullying.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each action.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: Project manager leads the team, treasurer keeps money records, production team makes the goods, sales team sells the goods.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each role and duty pair.
